pages.title: Models, Auth, Skills, and Plugins
pages.purpose: Model catalog and extension management: model runtime, provider auth (OAuth), credential vault in main and sync to host, skills service, plugins service and preflight.
instructions: Cover skills install/update (npm concurrency and isolated-cache retry) and plugins preflight policy checks.
Document the model directory refresh/caching failure semantics, browser OAuth login flow, and the vault round-trip between main and host.
Verify each behavior against the named .test.mjs files and cite them as focused tests.

pages.title: Agent Sessions and Event Streaming
pages.purpose: Core agent session flow: RPC handler registration, live session lifecycle in rpc-manager, session events, session file persistence/index/history, titles, compaction, file access roots.
instructions: Cover allowed-roots file access enforcement and the toolchain-aware bash/search tool wiring.
Explain how pi-coding-agent SessionManager/AgentSession objects are wrapped, how running-session events are streamed, and which stores persist what (session files, index, history, drafts, UI state).
Note the 2000-line handlers.ts as registration surface; focus on behavior, not enumeration.

pages.title: Host Lifecycle and Recovery
pages.purpose: HostManager supervision and failure handling: spawn/ready handshake, MessagePort forwarding, restart budget, heartbeat ping/pong, toolchain/browser snapshot ack synchronization, crash recovery, diagnostics.
instructions: Cover diagnostics export and redaction paths (diagnostics.ts, diagnostics-redaction.ts) and crashReporter configuration.
Cover the supervisor state machine: spawn, ready handshake, ping/pong liveness evaluation (shared/heartbeat-liveness), crash-window restart budget, port queueing, and pre-restart hook.
Include the pi version pinning (PI_DESKTOP_EXPECTED_PI_VERSION define in tsup.config.ts) and compatibility checker.

pages.title: Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: Process model and ownership boundaries: Electron main, preload, renderer, agent-host utility process, contract layer; how a user action flows end-to-end.
instructions: Describe the four execution contexts (main, preload, renderer, agent-host utility process plus nested workers) and who owns what, using file header comments and imports as evidence.
State that main.ts claims 'No business logic' and verify what that actually means from src/main code.
Trace one representative end-to-end flow (renderer sends RPC request -> host handler -> session event stream back) without exhaustively inventorying files.

pages.title: RPC Contract and IPC Trust
pages.purpose: Typed RPC contract and IPC trust model: wire protocol in src/contract/rpc.ts, Api method registry, desktop IPC channels, preload bridge, sender trust checks.
instructions: Cover renderer-side connection: where createRpcClient is used and how reconnection works.
Document the five wire message kinds, request timeout behavior, subscribe/event key model, and how the API surface type-checks are enforced (contract coverage checker).
Explain MessagePort transfer mechanics and the sandbox/contextIsolation invariants, citing preload comments and ipc-trust code.

pages.title: Browser Agent Tool Integration
pages.purpose: Agent-facing browser tooling: capability snapshot pushed to host, browser tool definitions, agent runtime calls into main BrowserService, authorization decisions and grants.
instructions: Cover CDP coordinator and advanced-mode identity/header rules from the agent-tool perspective.
Cover authorization coordinator handshake between host tool calls and main-process user confirmations.
Explain how BrowserCapabilitySnapshot reaches the host via HostManager messages and ack revisions, and how tools are re-synced on change.

pages.title: Embedded Browser Service
pages.purpose: Embedded browser (main process): BrowserService orchestration, tab/profile management, policy and network interception, downloads, header rules, secret vault, persistent grants, settings and restore stores.
instructions: Cover persistence locations (profiles, settings stores, snippets, restore store) and safeStorage usage for secrets.
Distinguish documented README claims (e.g. best-effort private network protection) from what the code enforces; state uncertainty where code does not establish a guarantee.
Examine the collaborator classes and their invariants: confirmation proofs, HMAC-signed grants if present, TTLs, and fail-closed behaviors.

pages.title: Desktop Shell and Auto-Updates
pages.purpose: Desktop shell and updates: window lifecycle and state, menus, tray, single-instance, deep links, custom protocol handlers, file associations, update manager/adapter, notifications and badges.
instructions: Cover the desktop:* IPC surface and the renderer-facing PiBridge contract.
Document what runs before app.whenReady and what single-instance/protocol registration requires.
Explain update state machine, platform gating (isProductionUpdatePlatformEnabled), and download/install-after-task semantics as implemented.

pages.title: Common Change Playbooks
pages.purpose: Focused change playbooks for representative maintenance tasks: adding an RPC API method end-to-end, adding a channel adapter, adding a toolchain capability, extending managed-process tools, and release checklist.
instructions: Each playbook must be grounded: name the exact files and checkers that must change together, citing where the invariant is enforced (e.g. contract coverage checker for API methods, i18n checker for renderer strings).
Prefer verified sequences over generic advice; run only read-only discovery commands while researching.
State explicitly when the repository does not establish a required step.

pages.title: IM Channel Integration
pages.purpose: IM channel integration: channel manager lifecycle, Feishu/Telegram/Weixin adapters, pairing/allowlist policy, Pi session bridge, media staging, lane scheduler, outbound rendering and redaction.
instructions: Cover secret handling (credential round-trip through main vault, redaction fingerprints).
List adapter capabilities and constraints honestly (e.g. WeChat group support, voice conversion) only as the code establishes them.
Trace inbound message -> policy evaluation -> PiSessionBridge turn -> outbound render/reply, including lane scheduling for concurrency.

pages.title: Managed Process Service and Workers
pages.purpose: Managed background processes (host side): managed-process service, per-process worker coprocess protocol, POSIX backend, agent tools, output buffers, session redaction.
instructions: Cover capability projection that gates tool exposure based on platform/reaper/helper/owner state.
Document the process tree: host service -> worker coprocess -> target process, the JSON request/event protocol, stop mode ladder, and output buffering/cursor semantics.
Explain owner identity handshake (hostInstanceId, main start fingerprint) and what fails closed when readiness is missing.

pages.title: Windows Helper and Process Reaping
pages.purpose: Windows helper and reaping: native Rust helper protocol and Job Object containment, main-process reaper, journal, shutdown cleanup, integrity/reproducibility verification.
instructions: Cover integrity verification of the helper binary and reproducibility checks.
Cover main-side reaper lifecycle, shutdown deadline cleanup, and fail-closed gating.
Explain the helper framing protocol, Job Object containment, and reaper journal semantics.

pages.title: Build and Release Pipeline
pages.purpose: Build and release pipeline: tsup/vite build targets, bundling invariants, electron-builder packaging, toolchain catalog provisioning, Windows helper build and reproducibility, SBOM, mac signing/notarization, CI workflow.
instructions: Cover mac signing/notarization script and Windows helper/SBOM verification gates; describe CI workflow triggers as configured.
Cover package-desktop flow, electron-builder files/extraResources rules and the reason for explicit FileSets.
Document tsup three-bundle layout and what stays external and why (comments in tsup.config.ts).

pages.title: Testing and Quality Gates
pages.purpose: Testing and quality gates: test runner and unit suite, verify.mjs gate order, contract coverage checker, security/dependency/i18n checkers, smoke and browser E2E harnesses.
instructions: Cover the Electron smoke and browser e2e harness modes and their prerequisites (e.g. display server needs).
Document each gate's purpose narrowly (what it fails on) citing its script.
Explain how tests are discovered/run and how .test.mjs colocated tests fit into the pipeline.

pages.title: Renderer Application
pages.purpose: Renderer application: React app structure, host connection from renderer side, session/chat state hooks, configuration screens, i18n and theme systems.
instructions: Cover the i18n dictionary invariants and offline asset constraints checked by scripts.
Focus on structural patterns and contracts rather than describing every component.
Trace how the renderer obtains the host MessagePort and builds its RPC client.

pages.title: Toolchain Discovery and Provisioning
pages.purpose: Developer toolchain management: discovery registry and probes, runtime catalog, private installer and secure extraction, shims, environment/PATH patching, snapshot propagation to the host.
instructions: Cover catalog JSON schema validation and bundled ripgrep/fd verification.
Document the discovery/probe/install pipeline and where private app storage paths come from.
Explain ToolchainSnapshot revisioning and application in the host (toolchain:ack), and how bash/git/search tools consume resolved executables.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Practical entry point: environment prerequisites, install, dev loop, build, test/verify, packaging, where to start for common maintenance tasks.
instructions: Cite package.json scripts and scripts/dev.mjs, scripts/verify.mjs spans; do not invent commands not present in package.json.
Cover: dev prerequisites (Node 22.19.x per package.json engines), npm install, npm run dev, npm test, npm run verify, build, pack/dist, and where to look first for common tasks.
